summary: myseliasan can now manage an adopted myiotsan sensor node directly from its own UI: a new nodeiot/ embed (mirroring the existing nodecam camera-node embed) renders that node's Devices/Rules/Alerts/Discovery/Commands pages inside myseliasan, tunneled entirely through the existing commander proxy (/api/nodes/{id}/proxy/...) so the browser never opens a connection to the node itself. Alongside this, myiotsan's device_command and alert_event audit rows now record the acting operator's name (RequestedByName / AckedByName), not just a local user id — a command or acknowledgement issued from the myseliasan control plane arrives with no account on the node (id 0), so without the name the node's own audit trail would say a relay was switched or an alert acknowledged by "System" instead of the person who actually did it.
compatibility: No schema migration needed for the new entity fields: RequestedByName/AckedByName are plain new columns created via the existing entity-driven bootstrap, default empty string for any pre-existing rows, and are purely additive to the existing DeviceCommand/AlertEvent JSON shape. Local (non-tunneled) commands and acks are unaffected in behavior; only the audit display gains the actor's name. The nodeiot embed adds no new API surface on myiotsan itself and requires no operator action to enable — it activates automatically for any node whose adopted Kind is "iot".
